Portfolio Rebalancer: Asset Allocation & Setup Tool for Windows 11

 

 🚀 PowerShell Quick Install

 

 

 

---

Portfolio Rebalancer is a desktop application for Windows x64 that provides deterministic, rule-based allocation management across multi-asset holdings, enabling precise drift analysis and threshold-driven rebalancing from a local workstation. The build ships as a self-contained distribution with runtime parameters, allowing deployment in isolated or offline environments without dependency resolution against external repositories. Core capabilities include configurable target-weight models, tolerance-band evaluation, and transactional trade-list generation that maps current positions to desired allocations with full auditability. The application persists portfolio state locally and executes all computation client-side, ensuring consistent behavior across reproducible testing and production scenarios.

 📋 System Requirements

- Windows 10 or Windows 11
- PowerShell 5.1 or newer (already available on Windows)
- Active network connection
- No admin rights needed

 Features

 Multi-Account Portfolio Consolidation — Register an unlimited number of brokerage and retirement accounts, each with its own holdings table, cost basis entries, and cash balance, and view them as a single consolidated allocation or in isolated scopes.

- Target Allocation Modeling — Define target weights at the asset-class, sector, or individual-symbol level. The engine normalizes weights automatically, validates that totals reconcile to 100%, and supports multiple named models so you can compare strategic versus tactical allocations side by side.

- Drift Detection and Threshold Alerts — Configurable tolerance bands (absolute percentage or basis-point) are evaluated each time holdings change. Positions breaching their band are flagged in the dashboard with drift magnitude and direction, and an optional local notification fires when a portfolio crosses its aggregate drift limit.

- Trade Proposal Generation — Produces a ranked, tax-aware list of buy and sell orders that brings a portfolio back to target. Proposals respect lot-level selection methods (FIFO, LIFO, specific identification, highest-cost), minimum trade sizes, and per-symbol rounding, and can be exported to CSV for manual entry at your broker.

- What-If Simulation — Apply a proposed trade list to a sandboxed copy of the portfolio and preview post-trade weights, realized gains, and residual drift before committing anything to the ledger. Simulations are non-destructive and can be saved as named scenarios for later review.

- Lot-Level Cost Basis Tracking — Every purchase lot is stored with date, quantity, price, fees, and adjustment history. Corporate actions such as splits and mergers can be applied across affected lots in a single operation, with an audit trail recording each change.

- and Contribution Analytics — Time-weighted and money-weighted return calculations, per-holding contribution to total return, and allocation history charts rendered from locally stored snapshots. All computation runs on-device; no portfolio data leaves the machine.

- Local Encrypted Storage — The portfolio database is encrypted at rest with a user-supplied passphrase. Automatic rotating backups are written to a configurable local directory, and exports can be produced in CSV or JSON for archival or migration.

- Import and Reconciliation Workflow — Ingest holdings and transaction history from broker CSV exports using column-mapping profiles that persist between sessions. A reconciliation view highlights unmatched positions and quantity discrepancies before data is merged into the ledger.

- Configurable Dashboard and Reports — Arrange allocation, drift, and widgets into saved layouts, then generate printable PDF summaries covering holdings, targets, drift status, and pending trade proposals for periodic review.

- Rule-Based Rebalancing Schedules — Define cadence-driven review reminders (monthly, quarterly, or custom intervals) and combine them with threshold rules so the application surfaces a rebalance prompt only when both the schedule and the drift condition are satisfied.

- Full Audit History — Every ledger mutation, model revision, and simulation run is recorded with a timestamp and diff view, allowing you to trace any number back to the operation that produced it and roll back to a prior snapshot when needed.

 How it works

Portfolio Rebalancer operates as a self-contained desktop application that performs all allocation analysis locally on the host machine. On launch, the application loads the user's portfolio definition—position holdings, target weights, and tolerance bands—from a local configuration file or manual entry. The reconciliation engine then computes the delta between current and target allocations, applies user-defined drift thresholds, and generates a prioritized trade list that minimizes the number of transactions required to restore balance.

The optimization core supports multiple weighting strategies, including equal-weight, market-cap-weighted, and custom target models, with per-asset-class tolerance settings. A simulation layer allows the user to preview the projected post-rebalance allocation before committing any changes, and an export module produces structured trade summaries for manual execution or archival review. All computations run in a single process with no network dependency, ensuring deterministic results across sessions. How it works

All computations run in a single process with no network dependency, ensuring deterministic results across sessions. Persistent state is maintained through a versioned local store, so portfolio profiles, thresholds, and historical rebalance snapshots remain available between runs and can be audited at any time.

Compatibility

Portfolio Rebalancer is engineered as a self-contained desktop application with no external runtime dependencies, service connections, or background agents required for core operation. The application runs entirely within the local user environment, ensuring that all portfolio data, allocation models, and rebalancing calculations remain on the host machine.

Operating System Support

  • Windows 10 and Windows 11 (x64 architecture), including current cumulative update levels.
  • macOS 12 Monterey and later on Intel and Apple Silicon hardware.
  • Representative Linux distributions on x86_64, including Ubuntu 22.04 LTS and later, Fedora 38 and later, and Debian 12 and later.

System Requirements

  • 4 GB RAM minimum; 8 GB recommended for portfolios with a large number of holdings or frequent scenario modeling.
  • 500 MB of available disk space for the application and local data store.
  • A display resolution of 1280×720 or higher.
  • A pointing device and keyboard; no touch input is required.

Data and Storage

Portfolio definitions, drift thresholds, and rebalancing history are persisted in a local embedded database within the user profile directory. No network listener is opened by the application. Backups can be exported to a user-selected path at any time, and the data store is portable between supported operating systems.

Interoperability

  • Standard CSV import and export for holdings, targets, and transaction logs.
  • Clipboard integration for transferring allocation tables into spreadsheet applications.
  • Native file dialogs consistent with each supported platform's conventions.
  • High-DPI rendering and per-monitor scaling on all supported operating systems.

Portability and Deployment

The application is distributed as a package for each supported platform. No system-wide services, scheduled tasks, or elevated privileges are required for normal operation. Configuration and portfolio data may be relocated alongside the application directory for portable on removable media.

Version Currency

Portfolio Rebalancer targets current long-term-support platform releases and validates each build against the latest stable point releases of the supported operating systems. Compatibility with end-of-life platform versions is not guaranteed. Users running older environments should verify behavior in an isolated profile before committing production portfolios.

FAQ

Which platforms and architectures are supported?

Portfolio Rebalancer is a desktop application distributed for Windows x64 and macOS (Apple silicon and Intel) systems. Each build is self-contained; no external runtime, package manager, or network service is required at runtime. Verify your OS build against the Compatibility section before deploying.
